theme: 3 terms on how Swift frees memory: the system that counts references, the normal reference that keeps an object alive, and two objects that never let go

terms.definition: A system in Swift that counts the references to each class instance and frees it when none are left.
terms.example: ARC freed `photo` as soon as I set it to `nil`.

terms.definition: A normal reference that keeps a class instance alive for as long as the reference exists.
terms.example: `b` is still a Strong Reference, so the photo stays in memory.

terms.definition: A problem where class instances hold Strong References to each other, so none of them is ever freed.
terms.example: `deinit` never runs, so I think we have a Retain Cycle.

video.description:
Learn to explain how Swift frees memory: ARC, Strong Reference & Retain Cycle, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
ARC - A system in Swift that counts the references to each class instance and frees it when none are left.
Strong Reference - A normal reference that keeps a class instance alive for as long as the reference exists.
Retain Cycle - A problem where class instances hold Strong References to each other, so none of them is ever freed.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift ARC, Strong Reference & Retain Cycle | Day 38
landscape.description:
Explain ARC, Strong Reference & Retain Cycle in Swift by listening to a real code chat between two iOS devs.
ARC, 강한 참조, 순환 참조 표현을 영어 대화로 익혀요.

ARC - A system in Swift that counts the references to each class instance and frees it when none are left.
한국어: ARC: 각 클래스 인스턴스를 가리키는 참조 수를 세고, 남은 참조가 없으면 해제하는 Swift의 시스템

Strong Reference - A normal reference that keeps a class instance alive for as long as the reference exists.
한국어: 강한 참조: 참조가 있는 동안 클래스 인스턴스를 메모리에 살려 두는 기본 참조

Retain Cycle - A problem where class instances hold Strong References to each other, so none of them is ever freed.
한국어: 순환 참조: 인스턴스들이 서로 강한 참조로 붙잡고 있어 어느 것도 해제되지 않는 문제

In this video, Mina and Jake sort out why an object is never freed, what keeps it alive and how two objects can hold each other, in a chat-style conversation, with the Swift code on screen.

landscape.hook: Can you explain these memory terms in English?

dialogue.title: Why is Dev never freed?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Jake, I set my `Dev` to `nil`, but `Dev freed` never prints.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then something still holds it. ARC frees an object only when no references are left.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: But nothing else uses it. I set my variable to `nil`!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Check `Team`. Its `lead` property points back to the `Dev`.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Oh. So `lead` is a Strong Reference?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yes. A normal property is a Strong Reference by default.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And `Dev` holds its `team` the same way.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. That's a Retain Cycle. Each one keeps the other alive.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So ARC can't free either of them?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Exactly. ARC counts references, and here the count never reaches zero.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: How do we break the Retain Cycle?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We change one side so it isn't a Strong Reference. Then `Dev freed` prints.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Who frees my objects in Swift?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: ARC does, once no references are left.
